name: Hadadezer
title: King of Zobah
summary: Hadadezer was the king of Zobah, an Aramean kingdom north of Israel. He was a powerful enemy of King David but was defeated in several battles. David's victories over Hadadezer helped establish Israel's dominance over much of the region.

keyEvents.title: David's First Victory Over Hadadezer
keyEvents.description: David defeated Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah, when Hadadezer went to restore his power at the Euphrates River. David captured a thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers.

keyEvents.title: Arameans from Damascus Come to Aid Hadadezer
keyEvents.description: When the Arameans from Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David struck down twenty-two thousand of them and stationed garrisons in Aram-Damascus.

keyEvents.title: David Takes War Booty from Hadadezer
keyEvents.description: David took the golden shields that Hadadezer's servants carried and brought them to Jerusalem. He also took a large amount of bronze from Hadadezer's cities.

keyEvents.title: King Toi sends gifts to David
keyEvents.description: When King Toi of Hamat heard that David had defeated all of Hadadezer's army, he sent his son to David with gifts of gold, silver, and bronze to congratulate him.

keyEvents.title: Hadadezer sends Arameans against Israel again
keyEvents.description: Hadadezer sent messengers and mobilized the Arameans from beyond the Euphrates. Shobach, Hadadezer's commander, led them, but David gathered all Israel and crossed the Jordan to meet them.

keyEvents.title: The final defeat at Helam
keyEvents.description: David defeated the Arameans at Helam. Shobach, Hadadezer's commander, was killed in battle. All the kings who were subject to Hadadezer made peace with Israel and became their subjects.
